runs.text: Woes to Scribes and Pharisees
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:
runs.originalText: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:

runs.text: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
runs.originalText: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

runs.text: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.
runs.originalText: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

runs.text: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads
runs.originalText: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads

runs.text: and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
runs.originalText: and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.

runs.text: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
runs.originalText: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.

runs.text: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,
runs.originalText: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,

runs.text: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
runs.originalText: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.

runs.text: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.
runs.originalText: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

runs.text: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
runs.originalText: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

runs.text: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.
runs.originalText: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.

runs.text: The greatest among you shall be your servant.
runs.originalText: The greatest among you shall be your servant.

runs.text: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
runs.originalText: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

runs.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
runs.originalText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.

runs.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell
runs.originalText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell

runs.text: as you are.

runs.text: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
runs.originalText: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’

runs.text: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?
runs.originalText: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?

runs.text: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’

runs.text: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
runs.originalText: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

runs.text: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.
runs.originalText: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.

runs.text: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.
runs.originalText: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.

runs.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.

runs.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.
runs.originalText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.

runs.text: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

runs.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.
runs.originalText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.

runs.text: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.
runs.originalText: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.

runs.text: Lament over Jerusalem

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

runs.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
